headline.label: Uptime
headline.detail: Productive time across 12 tools and 90 operational days.

headline.label: Availability (OEE)
headline.detail: Productive time over planned production time (scheduled maintenance excluded).

headline.label: Yield
headline.detail: Mean daily yield ± one standard deviation across tool-days.

summary_sentences: Across 12 tools over 90 operational days (Aug 21, 2026 to Nov 18, 2026), the fleet ran at 86.7% uptime with 328 unscheduled failures, MTBF 68.2 h and MTTR 0.93 h.
Fleet throughput averaged 42.6 wafers/hour (median 43.4, p95 57.9), while yield averaged 98.61% ± 0.59 across tool-days.
Tool TRACK-04 throughput averaged 43.3 wph over 90 days, 1.5% above the fleet mean; 7 of 90 days fell below the lower control limit (3σ), bottoming at 30.9 wph (-3.45σ) on Nov 05, 2026 (p < 0.001).
Tool SCANNER-02 yield averaged 98.47% over 90 days, 0.1% below the fleet mean; 5 of 90 days fell below the lower control limit (3σ), bottoming at 92.63% (-4.22σ) on Oct 26, 2026 (p < 0.001).
Tool TRACK-02 yield averaged 98.00% over 90 days, 0.6% below the fleet mean; 1 of 90 days fell below the lower control limit (3σ), bottoming at 97.90% (-3.49σ) on Nov 12, 2026.
9 of 15 fault codes account for 80% of 7,191 fault events; VAC_LOSS leads with 1,219 events (17.0%).
The largest handoff effect is C→A on SCANNER-02: higher by 8.6% (53.9 → 58.5), p < 0.001.

glossary.definition: Upper and lower control limits, drawn at the process mean ± 3 standard deviations; a point outside them is unlikely under stable random variation.
Mean time between failures: productive hours divided by the number of unscheduled-down episodes.
Mean time to repair: total unscheduled-down hours divided by the number of unscheduled-down episodes.
Interquartile range, the distance between the 25th and 75th percentiles; Tukey outliers lie beyond 1.5×IQR from the box.
The probability of seeing a difference at least this large if nothing real changed; below 0.05 is conventionally called significant.
Productive time divided by planned production time, excluding scheduled maintenance but including standby, engineering and unplanned downtime.
The average of a metric over a trailing window of days, used to separate signal from day-to-day noise.
